messages:

Subject: Notice: LogStream (subprocessor) onboarding for EdgeWave feed ingestion

Hi Hiro / Laura,

Per our contract (Order Form #EW-1120) we have a new subprocessor to support the log-ship pipeline: LogStream, Inc. They will handle ingestion and short-term buffering for EdgeWave-managed logs. We wanted to share the materials you requested for the flow-down review and to kick off the approval path.

Attached: LogStream_subproc_factsheet.pdf (scope + data elements), flowdown_mapping_matrix.xlsx (clauses we propose to flow down), redlined_MSA_EdgeWave_v2.docx (vendor redlines to the MSA).

Requested next steps from your side:
- Confirmation of evidence bucket required (SOC2 Type II, encryption in transit & at rest attestation, IL/retention specifics).
- Any DPA annex language we should accept or further redline (we included a proposed DPA excerpt in the redline).
- Route for procurement/legal signoff and estimated SLA for review (we're aiming for expedited approval next week).

Samir Shah (LogStream technical lead) and our legal team are on copy for any technical or legal clarifications.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Price

Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: LogStream (subprocessor) onboarding for EdgeWave feed ingestion

Jordan — thanks for the heads up and the package. Quick acknowledgement from our side and a few clarifying asks so procurement/legal/security can triage efficiently:

1) Evidence bucket: procurement will need SOC2 Type II report (most recent), a completed security questionnaire (we'll attach our standard SIG-lite), and an encryption attestation that lists KMS usage and key rotation cadence.
2) Data residency & retention: confirm whether LogStream will have access to raw PII (we expect redaction at source for any user identifiers). If they will retain logs beyond 30 days, procurement will require retention carveouts in the order form.
3) Flowdown scope: the matrix looks reasonable but Kimberly, can you confirm whether the proposed DPA excerpt in the redline covers our audit log preservation and breach notification SLAs?
4) Temporary mitigation: if legal needs extra time, can EdgeWave limit LogStream to pseudonymous logs only for a 30-day onboarding window?

If you can provide the SOC2 report and the completed SIG-lite by EOD tomorrow, we can try to get procurement and security to review on Wednesday. Laura — can procurement own the evidence collection? Kimberly — please prioritize a redline pass on the DPA clauses (I'll ping you offline with clause numbers). Rishi — can you confirm whether the suggested limited-scope onboarding (pseudonymous mode) is technically enforceable from our side?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — this feed is time-sensitive for the EdgeWave integration.

Best,
Hiro Tanaka
Senior Partner Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick updates:

- SOC2: attached (redacted for customer names) — LogStream completed their Type II audit in April 2026.
- SIG-lite: attached a filled copy; we left a few architecture notes where we need vendor clarification.
- Retention: LogStream will retain raw ingestion for up to 14 days by default, 90 days only with a contractual exception. They do not process direct end-user PII by default; identifiers are hashed at ingest.
- DPA redlines: we've included a DPA excerpt in redlined_MSA_EdgeWave_v2.docx. EdgeWave legal prefers to flow down breach notification timelines to subprocessor as-is; they note that some of the Redwood proposed carveouts were flagged.

DocuSign: we can push an amendment/order-form for the limited onboarding scope if you prefer — link: https://www.docusign.com/Envelope/ABC-123-EDGEWAVE

Attachments included: redlined_MSA_EdgeWave_v2.docx (vendor redlines + DPA excerpt), LogStream_SOC2_Apr2026_redacted.pdf, SIG-lite_LogStream_filled.xlsx, flowdown_mapping_matrix.xlsx

Jordan

Fyi — forwarding the vendor package. My initial read and recommended next steps:

On Tue, Jul 6, 2026 at 13:46, Jordan Price <jordan.price@edgewave.com> wrote:
> [vendor attachments omitted in inline forwarding]
>
> - SOC2 looks current; we'll need the full report for redaction review.
> - Retention default of 14 days is acceptable; anything beyond must be explicitly enumerated in Order Form.
> - Vendor redlines: they have pushed back on our audit log preservation language (Clause 6.4); we should push for a limited-scope acceptance: preserve audit logs for services that impact customer data flows, otherwise narrower logging is OK.

Kimberly's recommended actions:
1) Procurement (Laura) to collect the full SOC2 report and SIG artifacts and attach to the HubSpot record. Do not approve until we have the full SOC2 and SOC2 bridge or compensating evidence.
2) Security (Rishi) to validate LogStream's KMS usage and confirm whether server-side hashing meets our pseudonymization requirement; if not, require hashing at source in EdgeWave pipeline.
3) Legal (me) will propose two limited redline options to vendor: (A) Accept DPA excerpt with clarified audit log scope + 30-day onboarding pseudonymous-only window, or (B) Accept full flowdown but require DocuSign amendment that ties retention to each Order Form extension.
4) If EdgeWave agrees to pseudonymous-only onboarding, allow limited ingress while procurement completes evidence collection.

I'll draft the two redline options and share for internal review by EOD Thursday. Laura — please mirror hubspot record to this thread once you have the SOC2 file. Rishi — flag if you see any blocking encryption gaps; otherwise I'll proceed with option (A) draft.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
